dish: a modern French tasting menu with Japanese accents (Trier's only Michelin star)
w: On the picturesque Zurlaubener Ufer, this is Trier's single Michelin-starred kitchen, held since 2023 and defended every year. Chef Gerald Schöberl, a former sous-chef to three-star Christian Bau, marries classic French technique with subtle Japanese touches — the fine-dining benchmark of the oldest city in Germany.

dish: Harald Rüssel's produce-driven German tasting menu with self-hunted game
w: In a quiet side valley of the Mosel between Trier and Leiwen, chef-patron Harald Rüssel has held a Michelin star (17 Gault&Millau points) since the early 1990s. The gourmet restaurant celebrates German produce at the highest level — the kitchen even hunts its own game — with a rustic Hasenpfeffer country-restaurant alongside.

dish: a classic-modern French menu on the Mosel in a Jugendstil hotel
w: The kitchen of the landmark Art-Nouveau Hotel Bellevue, right on the river in Traben-Trarbach, listed in the Michelin guide and by Der Feinschmecker. Classic-modern, French-inspired cooking (a five-course menu around 100 euro) with a strong Mosel wine list and a terrace over the water.

dish: French cuisine in a 17th-century half-timbered house with Mosel wines
w: An elegant French restaurant set in a historic half-timbered house on the Burgstraße in old-town Bernkastel-Kues, with rooms at the Gästehaus am Schlossberg. A long-standing Falstaff-listed address, and one of the highest-rated tables in the town.

dish: house-brewed Kraft Bräu craft beer with regional cooking (Trier's first brewpub)
w: A family-run 4-star hotel on the road out to the Olewig vineyards whose Kraft Bräu, founded 1998, was the first house brewery in Trier — a beer pub and large beer garden alongside an upscale a la carte restaurant. Fresh, largely regional and organic cooking paired with award-winning craft beers, the local answer to the city's wine.

dish: Ruwer estate Riesling with Hochwald game and local brook trout (ERBEN von Beulwitz)
w: In the romantic Ruwer valley on Trier's edge, this restaurant links the wines of the family estate ERBEN von Beulwitz to regional cuisine. Head chef Bernd Schneider builds relaxed, high-quality menus around Hochwald game, brook trout from local waters and regional cheese — a wine-hotel table for the Mosel's Ruwer tributary.

dish: Leiwener Laurentiuslay and Piesporter Goldtröpfchen Riesling at the estate (Nik Weis)
w: A leading VDP-calibre family estate above Leiwen, run by Nik Weis in the third generation, with holdings in top Middle-Mosel sites including the Leiwener Laurentiuslay and Piesporter Goldtröpfchen. Tastings at the winery are one of the best ways to drink steep-slate Riesling at source in the heart of the Mittelmosel.

dish: Saar Riesling from VDP.Grosse Lage sites at the hilltop vinothek
w: One of the Saar's most important estates, VDP-classified and revived by Roman Niewodniczanski into one of Germany's largest private wineries, almost entirely Riesling from old vines. Its striking new winery and vinothek stand high above the Saar near the Ayler Kupp — a destination tasting for Grand-Cru Saar Riesling.

dish: regional Mosel cooking with a Riesling wine bar in the old town hall
w: In the historic old town hall directly on Bernkastel's picture-book market square, serving regional dishes in modern surroundings. Evenings bring the wine bar 'Tresor Wine & Bar' with regional selections by the glass — a central, wine-forward stop in the Middle Mosel's most-visited town.

dish: handmade Torten and confiserie from a four-generation Konditorei
w: A traditional family Konditorei-Confiserie in Trier's centre, in the same family for four generations and listed by both Falstaff and Der Feinschmecker. The classic old-town address for Kaffee und Kuchen, cakes and handmade confectionery.

dish: Trier-Olewig estate Riesling with a vintner's plate in the Weinstube
w: A family winery and wine tavern in Trier's Olewig wine district, run by the Schleimer family for three generations just minutes from the city centre. Its Weinstube pours the estate's own Riesling with vintner's cooking — an authentic way to taste Trier as a working wine town.

dish: Laurentiuslay and Goldtröpfchen Riesling, incl. Grosses Gewächs, at the VDP estate
w: A VDP estate growing wine in Leiwen since 1624, with parcels in the Leiwener Laurentiuslay, Trittenheimer Apotheke and Piesporter Goldtröpfchen, some 85% Riesling. A serious address for dry Grosses Gewächs and fine noble-sweet Mosel Riesling on one of the river's grandest loops.
